![IMG_0597.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/242rwANfanKquNCJzy2jQ1gmvJxZkDPrUrCiiRP97QvVeW2JrcfWGqK1iWKHdtsMvxCdU.jpeg)
[Léelo en **español** aquí](#spanish)

Oh my god - did you see that the next Hivefest has been announced? It will be in Barcelona, Spain - and we are already so excited to join the party. But first things first - to get a little taste of what it may be like, we went to The Hive Open Days in Alicante two weeks ago. Yes - As you may know, the Hive Community came back together on a big event already this year. And as always, it was a great pleasure, very interesting, and so much fun to meet Hiveans from all over the world, sharing and exchanging thoughts and ideas about the ecosystem and its initiatives. Every single time the Hive Community comes together in person, feeling the spirit is so special. Here you can truly feel what Hive is about (at least for us) - and of course what Worldmappin is about. -> bringing people from all over the world together to talk about the future! So here is a little report about what happened that days for those of you that couldn´t join: # Day 1 - Waterproof stickers for everyone! ![IMG_9657.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xKxvXLX2WNfSJJTXN61rJn7hoViGpT4fMSMD32RAUShs8pqqK62oZDmA4LD3LaHMCLD.jpeg)|![IMG_0758.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23wC9iMVbV9SeWMetZM6WzNJWWUSVQkGHSinqPeJ6g1k2MHuQPztSpcV9apFHupDkbEPg.jpeg) --|-- ![IMG_9822.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23vi62BL7bC2CspiLUmCFhtWsCieoLKsa9MvtCDhnMNk2R6rCdGUpcaT718b6g4ZWoWTk.jpeg)|![IMG_9846.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23u65K3zjk5PK99ybg9amYX9bKEtZySPJ3H78MACfscqG7CX6UXa97jdwYy6tSAiyJChH.jpeg)| ![IMG_9717.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23uFc5xsvmXgiAKvSX11N1eDBFDHn5MybfuzH8S6V2khLMCUuWegKNyKdqmigbdzMQqqa.jpeg) ---|---|--- We were there from the very first day of #HODAlicante, greeting and welcoming both Hive users and attendees from outside the ecosystem. For some Hivians, it was even their first time experiencing an event of this kind, so #worldmappin was there representing one of Hive’s largest and most active communities—one that strives to engage with its users and make them feel connected. We came to this event packed with new features, one of which was handing out hundreds of waterproof #worldmappin pin stickers. We’d done some tests beforehand that showed good results, and now we’ve brought this version for everyone—in two sizes—which is even more weather-resistant and ensures greater longevity for users who mark locations on our map to document their visits. The feedback was incredible, as many users mentioned that they had thought about durability when leaving the #worldmappin stamp around the world. So, after the official presentations, we went out with several users around the city, stamping the badge in various places for testing! *Thanks @honeydue for helping us out with that! # Day 2 - New version of WMP and upcoming goals ![IMG_0570.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23w2oVKKsbNoswCPk5Ex8ae79WH1LBwetA7a8K1AqafGEHYHhsQE5W1E7AGQ2kvi6JVT9.jpeg) The second day of the event was dedicated to official presentations about the Hive ecosystem: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6I4M0ap6vA We had the great responsibility of closing the event, so we decided to focus on two main aspects: welcoming the new Hivians who created their accounts the day before the event, introducing them to the project as a useful tool for their new journey within Hive, and devoting a large part of the presentation to a tour of all the new features we’ve been working on lately. We showcased all the new features of the recently launched [WorldMappin V2](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@worldmappin/exciting-news-worldmappin-v2-is-live), the project’s new face. We thanked all the users who have helped us so much with their feedback, showing how we’ve incorporated into our interface the details and tools that users care about most, letting them know that this is just the beginning of the new phase of #WorldMappin and that we’ll keep working to bring improvements for everyone. So now you know—don’t hesitate to support our proposal ([Peakd.com](https://peakd.com/proposals/348) / [Ecency](https://ecency.com/proposals/348) / [Hive.blog](https://wallet.hive.blog/proposals/348) / [HiveSigner](https://hivesigner.com/sign/update_proposal_votes?proposal_ids=%5B%22348%22%5D&approve=true)) to help us keep working on this wonderful project. ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23vsb96t8FUyD4PHBgWGgVsiRcVRhGcysGhssvSeWsT3UdBacjsKqKNUsasCyuFsFzf2S.jpeg) ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tvsFr9j1Xcf1cfv9XSXsZZjcidKUhBdEod6FjUYSV8qP1XmQTP2FhfcGtVGr3k3ghLn.jpeg) ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xpAnfLHxz3NWN1WkoszCo4niSbU1apobHUwiA6MTkWjZU4VJFbPvVTx3egajonM2JE4.jpeg) Another highlight of the day, which we joined in celebrating with the @mantequilla-soft team, was putting into practice the wonderful real-time translation tool that @tibfox brought to the event and made available to all speakers, thereby helping everyone understand the information being shared even if they didn’t speak the language. The mobile app also provided access to many more languages to facilitate live translation for each user and, to allow them to have private conversations in different languages, breaking down that barrier that can sometimes be so frustrating. On our side, @ninaeatshere put it to the test by presenting our talk in Spanish, to make the information accessible to new Spanish-speaking users and, of course, to honor the place where we were, as we know that the Spanish-speaking community is a major part of our HIVE ecosystem and also of our Worldmappin Community. ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Ep5mHUbDd3Ezbng5Z5FvU8ro9ioGtm4PsfHu7H8L2pXczpxU3o8oZF8a6y24Rj63su3.jpeg)|![IMG_0599.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23yTji5XrrfTaYmqBTuauKZD4hX89iGrhG24wRUXGgabw9E8v8EqtYMGmwVfpvKJsQaUT.jpeg) --|-- ![IMG_0565.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xAgVEX4cDLxh9tceSAKZcP8rvmELVWLuKGJAkTQcHCuWBCWEycyFoTuxUMdxPMf6DSt.jpeg) ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/242DdHTEeAUveRsP2jhbSGqUgN2MCSgcgYweSimVrZrswdEqT1ZJnJrytzAQ4RXx3AGWW.jpeg) # Day 3 - Sponsoring the Clean Planet Challenge prizes! ![IMG_0087.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23zS5cQx5t1QrU8aesdsJc4dobjET49MBVkLLTzwVZNWGqBPsbBMXgdzuRE28d2kWwoLC.jpeg) Just like every year, during the #BuzzParty events organized by @tibfox, the wonderful #CleanPlanetChallenge took place, and of course, we were there to explore the island where it was held, plant a few pins in the surrounding area, and also motivate the participants with some backpacks full of Hive goodies for the challenge winners. Our team was there for the challenge, helping to clean up Tabarca Island, but, above all, encouraging participants to compete in a healthy spirit. That day, after @ninaeatshere took the pin out to eat, the team made sure to be present throughout the challenge so we could ultimately reward those who put in the most effort that afternoon. The keeper of the prizes was @godfish, who kept a watchful eye on everyone involved and presented the prizes to that day’s winning team. We handed out backpacks filled with goodies to the team of @gissse and @juanmatrader, two of the new users who fully immersed themselves in the Hive experience! ![IMG_0011.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Eoc8QckLcLNQCYJFG5eT1HmKrBND8PwapeoGr5V9SK7gtmZC2iSgdJBhkAMeG9gDig9.jpeg) ![IMG_0029.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EoEtN2zHRJ11zVJ5s2Jv8j1r5MuV6wi38tiBPqh6hsVqqLpiyX7U8VAwNXr3fSmANqT.jpeg) ![IMG_0595.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23yThC4RP9VMjYMWEQsS75TqvcoWbAoeJDsYnAEGfJSXZ2bctiwLe7Q66BDa75pPcECqH.jpeg)|![IMG_0117.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23y8zTpy6DdrCB1C66dLv9yLcaWbNop1QeY9nM5d7WD2brADsrcNYPpqw37QDSkHvRaUg.jpeg) --|-- ![IMG_0105.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23yd85xf1MTamt39PatWojHu7XVXU8PW8qGniSoHiUd8bBDA2tHiT8pJot6QJrSkeCqTS.jpeg) # Day 4 - Exploring the city with riddles! ![IMG_0249.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Eoke1Pn2xPKfhG6DYsrhQueoi6MoTb1VvcjQBLMLSvmob8Q8dnmVkGpirywauFZFZrh.jpeg) For our final day at #HODAlicante, we wanted to take event attendees on a tour of part of the city, immerse them in Alicante’s culture, and encourage them to post their travel content in the [WorldMAppin community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-163772/created). The goal of the tour was to visit some of Alicante’s landmarks while @ninaeatshere quizzed our dear Hivians with some travel riddles. It was the last day of the event, and attendees were really exhausted from the previous days; plus, there were local festivities in the city that limited our schedule and access to certain places, so we decided to take it easy, scale back the itinerary a bit, and ask very simple questions for the challenge. We met at the entrance to Ulab, the convention center where the talks took place, and headed out to visit three nearby spots:
**The Basilica of Santa María**
![IMG_0253.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EprV5sqGSt9pYQYvNrFmVgBg5dxUBoLv3gkQopS7mPkqHTjCzmSjDmQYY3KzPP2Knrh.jpeg)
**The Alicante Museum of Contemporary Art**
![IMG_0267.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EouBcgcUNP56YECZEydKKTsweNhz4bNfSnuwC7su4hr9p26tRrMwDx4J2Bz16BYx4qG.jpeg)
**Santa Cruz Cultural District**
![IMG_0303.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Ep7s6UvvnDYqqizYxFMbxZaC6wSfQLfotftCJn1LKuVKvffB1Pi55HSQsc6thmgJ1nU.jpeg)
😃 **The Santa Cruz Viewpoint is labeled with a WorldMappin pin**
![IMG_0298.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23x1DBQZdwN3VBYtEa9VqiyJz98W9nEPwwjAJ1PxzqmZkPrMSKUnp4iKxm5nMnmB3JaUT.jpeg) Since the end of the walk involved carrying our bags, we stopped to rest outside one of the picturesque little houses in the Santa Cruz neighborhood, where @godfish—the keeper of the prizes—was conveniently staying, and we settled in to share some snacks and hand out prizes to the three winners of the riddles we’d posed along the way. This time, another new user emerged as a winner: @anamz took home one of our backpacks full of prizes, accompanied by the victorious @edje and @palomap3 for being the fastest at solving the riddles that day. Here’s a photo of the scene where we raided @godfish’s place to award the three winners on the final leg of the journey. Some winners enthusiastically shared the contents of the famous backpack, so here’s a glimpse of what was inside. In the backpack, we included a couple of T-shirts: one from the previous HiveFest we sponsored and our nice black T-shirt. The winners also took home a good batch of Hive stickers, a water bottle, a small wallet (the **cold wallet**), and a couple of packets of **summer flower seeds**—a nice promotional initiative with a real purpose ( [click here](https://peakd.com/hive-121566/@detlev/hive-merch-with-results-smart-seed-marketing) if you’re interested in learning more about **Hive Seeds** or if you’re one of the winners and want to find out how to plant them) ![IMG_0282.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EoGyrB1vUGaXZCWmkedUj9MFSrBLt23FHxiitcm9quYrz3zd8QwnpW71dABNtuVdofq.jpeg) ![4e179531-2ae5-4ccf-a3f7-90d594b4477c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23w2eJgxLW3SpsJcUSkaaJRRLXnCuBUNpFgAwtUsQxEpXPDmD1iX9cdQ26cfeTs4HCyUb.jpeg)| ![77e48ea0-b9c8-4a07-af1c-6b36393790f5.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23w2ktvC2bvrftTrUvWbu4wXgUARuALsamMPYJFM6fCSrsxRhkThRSA88sAqX8vtuD4cR.jpeg) --|-- (Photos by winners Ana and Paloma) The WorldMAppin team is extremely grateful and proud to be able to participate in events like this one, which are full of initiatives that encourage users of our ecosystem to engage more deeply with the blockchain in various ways. We are pleased to say that we thoroughly enjoyed sharing this experience once again with the event organizers and all the users who attended. We want the users to feel close to us and to know that they can reach out to the team with any questions, suggestions, or feedback. It was a pleasure to be in Alicante, and we can’t wait to see you all again at the upcoming [HiveFest XI – Barcelona, the Heart of Catalonia! September 17–20, 2026](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@hivefest/save-the-date-hivefest-xi-barcelona-the-heart-of-catalonia-17-20-sept-2026). Until then, travelers! — **The Worldmappin Team** ![IMG_0525.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpxqFqjZsep8TjMMivRoVu33HCzReFCLxkd8yybw3GS6RK1LnXfGb7AoLx9B9CZqbgu.jpeg) *Photo credits: We would like to thank @ninaeatshere, @gisse, @schmidi, @haastrecht, @palomap3, and @anamz for sharing the photos featured in this post.*

**Español** ![IMG_0597.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/242rwANfanKquNCJzy2jQ1gmvJxZkDPrUrCiiRP97QvVeW2JrcfWGqK1iWKHdtsMvxCdU.jpeg) ¡Dios mío! ¿Ya vieron que se ha anunciado el próximo Hivefest? Se celebrará en Barcelona, ​​España, ¡y ya estamos sumamente emocionados por unirnos a la fiesta! Pero lo primero primero: para hacernos una idea de cómo podría ser, asistimos a los *Hive Open Days* en Alicante hace dos semanas. Sí; como tal vez ya sepan, la comunidad de Hive volvió a reunirse en un gran evento este mismo año. Y, como siempre, fue un inmenso placer —además de una experiencia muy interesante y tremendamente divertida— conocer a *Hiveans* de todas partes del mundo, compartiendo e intercambiando pensamientos e ideas sobre el ecosistema y sus iniciativas. Cada vez que la comunidad de Hive se reúne en persona, resulta verdaderamente especial sentir ese espíritu. Aquí es donde realmente se puede percibir la esencia de Hive (al menos para nosotros) y, por supuesto, la esencia de Worldmappin: ¡unir a personas de todo el mundo para conversar sobre el futuro! Así que, aquí les dejamos un breve resumen de lo que pasó durante esos días, pensado especialmente para aquellos de ustedes que no pudieron asistir: # Día 1: ¡Pegatinas resistentes al agua para todos! ![IMG_9657.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xKxvXLX2WNfSJJTXN61rJn7hoViGpT4fMSMD32RAUShs8pqqK62oZDmA4LD3LaHMCLD.jpeg)|![IMG_0758.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23wC9iMVbV9SeWMetZM6WzNJWWUSVQkGHSinqPeJ6g1k2MHuQPztSpcV9apFHupDkbEPg.jpeg) --|-- ![IMG_9822.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23vi62BL7bC2CspiLUmCFhtWsCieoLKsa9MvtCDhnMNk2R6rCdGUpcaT718b6g4ZWoWTk.jpeg)|![IMG_9846.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23u65K3zjk5PK99ybg9amYX9bKEtZySPJ3H78MACfscqG7CX6UXa97jdwYy6tSAiyJChH.jpeg)| ![IMG_9717.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23uFc5xsvmXgiAKvSX11N1eDBFDHn5MybfuzH8S6V2khLMCUuWegKNyKdqmigbdzMQqqa.jpeg) ---|---|--- Estuvimos presentes desde el primer día del #HODAlicante saludando y dando la bienvenida tanto a usuarios de Hive como a las personas externas al ecosistema que asistieron a las jornadas. Incluso para algunos Hivians era la primera vez que experimentaban un encuentro de este estilo, asi que #worldmappin estuvo allí representando a una de las comunidades mas grandes y activas de Hive que mas intenta involucrarse con sus usuarios y hacerse sentir cercana. Para este evento vinimos full de novedades, siendo una de ellas el reparto de cientos de pegatinas resistentes al agua del pin de #worldmappin, habiamos hecho algunas pruebas antes mostrando buenos resultados y ahora hemos traido esta version para todos, en dos tamaños, que es mucho mas resistente a la intemperie y le asegura mas longevidad a los usuarios que registran lugares en nuestro mapa reseñando sus visitas. El feedback fue increible, pues muchos usuarios manifestaron haber pensado en el aspecto de la durabilidad cuando dejaban la estampa de #worldmappin por el mundo, así que después de las presentaciones oficiales, nos fuimos junto a varios usuarios por la ciudad estampando el sello en varios lugares para hacer las pruebas correspondientes! # Día 2: Nueva versión y próximos objetivos ![IMG_0570.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23w2oVKKsbNoswCPk5Ex8ae79WH1LBwetA7a8K1AqafGEHYHhsQE5W1E7AGQ2kvi6JVT9.jpeg) El segundo día del evento estuvo dedicado a presentaciones oficiales sobre el ecosistema de Hive y nosotros tuvimos la gran responsabilidad de cerrar el evento, por lo que decidimos enfocarnos en dos aspectos principales, dar la bienvenida a los nuevos Hivians que crearon su nueva cuenta el día anterior del evento, presentandoles el proyecto como una herramienta util para su nuevo viaje dentro de Hive y, además, dedicamos gran parte del discurso a hacer un tour por todas las novedades en las que hemos estado trabajando ultimamente. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6I4M0ap6vA Mostramos todas las nuevas caracteristicas de la recien lanzada [WorldMappin V2](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@worldmappin/exciting-news-worldmappin-v2-is-live), la nueva cara del proyecto. Agradecimos a todos los usuarios que tanto nos han ayudado con su feedback, mostrando como hemos incluido a nuestra interfaz esos detalles y herramientas que tanto interesan a los usuarios, dejandoles saber que esto es solo el comienzo de la nueva etapa de #WorldMappin y que vamos a seguir trabajando en traer mejoras para todos. Asi que ya lo sabes, no dudes en apoyar nuestra propuesta ([Peakd.com](https://peakd.com/proposals/348) / [Ecency](https://ecency.com/proposals/348) / [Hive.blog](https://wallet.hive.blog/proposals/348) / [HiveSigner](https://hivesigner.com/sign/update_proposal_votes?proposal_ids=%5B%22348%22%5D&approve=true)) para ayudarnos a seguir trabajando en este proyecto tan bonito. ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23vsb96t8FUyD4PHBgWGgVsiRcVRhGcysGhssvSeWsT3UdBacjsKqKNUsasCyuFsFzf2S.jpeg) ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tvsFr9j1Xcf1cfv9XSXsZZjcidKUhBdEod6FjUYSV8qP1XmQTP2FhfcGtVGr3k3ghLn.jpeg) ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xpAnfLHxz3NWN1WkoszCo4niSbU1apobHUwiA6MTkWjZU4VJFbPvVTx3egajonM2JE4.jpeg) Otro aspecto en el que nos involucramos ese dia y celebramos junto al equipo de @mantequilla-soft fue poner en practica el uso de la maravillosa herramienta de traducción directa que nos trajo @tibfox al evento y a disposición de todos los oradores, para facilitar asi la comprensión de la información transmitida a pesar de no hablar el idioma. La aaplicación movil además permitía acceso a muchos mas idiomas para facilitar la traducción en vivo a cada usuario y, además, para que estos mantuvieran conversaciones particulares en distintos idiomas rompiendo esa barrera que a veces resulta tan molesta. Por nuestra parte @ninaeatshere hizo el test presentando nunestra charla en español, para facilitar la información a los nuevos usuarios españoles y, por supuesto, para honrar el lugar en donde estamos, pues sabemos que la comunidad hispanoablante es gran parte de nuestro ecosistema. ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Ep5mHUbDd3Ezbng5Z5FvU8ro9ioGtm4PsfHu7H8L2pXczpxU3o8oZF8a6y24Rj63su3.jpeg)|![IMG_0599.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23yTji5XrrfTaYmqBTuauKZD4hX89iGrhG24wRUXGgabw9E8v8EqtYMGmwVfpvKJsQaUT.jpeg) --|-- ![IMG_0565.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xAgVEX4cDLxh9tceSAKZcP8rvmELVWLuKGJAkTQcHCuWBCWEycyFoTuxUMdxPMf6DSt.jpeg) ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/242DdHTEeAUveRsP2jhbSGqUgN2MCSgcgYweSimVrZrswdEqT1ZJnJrytzAQ4RXx3AGWW.jpeg) # Día 3: ¡Patrocinando los premios del «Clean Planet Challenge»! ![IMG_0087.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23zS5cQx5t1QrU8aesdsJc4dobjET49MBVkLLTzwVZNWGqBPsbBMXgdzuRE28d2kWwoLC.jpeg) Como cada año, durante las #BuzzParty organizadas por @tibfox, se llevó a cabo el maravilloso reto #CleanPlanetChallenge y, por supuesto, estuvimos allí para recorrer juntos la isla en que este se llevo a cabo, anclar unos cuantos pines en los alrededores y además motivar a los participantes con unas mochilas llenas de Hive goodies para los ganadores del reto. Nuestro equipo estuvo presente en el reto, ayudando a limpiar la Isla de Tabarca pero sobre todo, motivando a los participantes a competir sanamente entre ellos. Ese día luego de que @ninaeatshere llevara nuestro pin a comer, el equipo se encargó de estar presente durante todo el reto para al final premiar a los que más se esforzaron esa tarde. El guardían de los premios fue @godfish, nuestro responsable de apoyo al Modelo de Negocio, quien mantuvo ojo avisor sobre cada involucrado y facilitó los pemios a la familia ganadora de ese día. ### English _______ # An Exotic, Cultural, and Religious Hike in Vietnam ______ Hello, dear friends! I hope you’re having a great day. Today I want to tell you about Vung Tau, in Vietnam. When I was in that country, this was one of my favorite places to visit, and the hike to the Christ statue was the part I enjoyed the most. I arrived in Vung Tau partly to escape the noise and skyscrapers of Saigon—now Ho Chi Minh City—and I took the ferry. I loved this place because it was incredibly authentic; it hadn’t been overrun by mass tourism, and it was surrounded by nature. It’s not a highly developed city—let’s say it’s small—but it has restaurants, trails, and beautiful boardwalks. One really beautiful thing is that on one side of the coast, on Little Hill (Núi Nhỏ), there’s a Christ statue watching over the area; there’s also a giant Buddha watching from the mountain, and on the other side, right across from it, is the Virgin Mary holding the baby Jesus in her arms. I found this amazing because it’s the only place in the world—at least that I’ve seen—where Buddhism and Catholicism coexist in such a vivid way.
> ### Español ______ > # Un trekking exótico, cultural y religioso en Vietnam ______ > Hola, queridos amigos! Espero que estén teniendo un gran día. Hoy les quiero hablar de Vung Tau, en Vietnam. Cuando estuve en ese país, uno de mis lugares preferidos para visitar fue justamente este, y específicamente la caminata hacia el Cristo fue la que a mí más me gustó. > Llegué a Vung Tau un poco escapando del ruido y los edificios de Saigón —actualmente Ho Chi Minh— y lo hice en ferry. Me encantó este sitio porque era sumamente auténtico, no estaba tan golpeado por el turismo masivo y además tenía mucha naturaleza. No llega a ser una ciudad demasiado desarrollada; digamos que es pequeña, pero cuenta con restaurantes, senderos y paseos marítimos preciosos. Algo muy bonito es que de un lado de la costa, en el Cerro Pequeño (Núi Nhỏ), hay un Cristo protegiendo; también hay un Buda gigante que cuida desde la montaña y, del otro lado, justo enfrente, está la Virgen María con el niño Jesús en brazos. Esto me pareció alucinante porque es el único lugar en el mundo, al menos que yo haya visto, donde conviven de una manera tan viva el budismo con el catolicismo.
________________________ ![IMG_1316.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EptcPXMXjtLBshrwJinjqiWTbSBk6SiApSBmNV2yPwjKhxxCaoWQvd19Lks3EsQpBiz.jpeg) ![IMG_1314.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqJ1JMmLGzuiq73kVaz2C4fkc7751zj3NriGD7V6pk2zf2GKzKUQ2n6o3FqJyMfNt2k.jpeg) ![IMG_1317.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpT64PhoH9Br2Z2effZYiwFzNyejyMiXwP2dpacgJCAssMhyMLk3u1VyKppCoLpm65T.jpeg) ![IMG_1322.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/Eos2K5iUspNhKG7s642xawXMvbve9KF6Vu713o4RMuYKRBjpGjYHnBaEPfV9DA8PXBv.jpeg) ![IMG_1319.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/Eptby9vK9fQwQwMYDW6ZdgXhG5EcDZZYjZrdF5E2kBUEWcj5U4S2WM1CLPw3WMm6mz2.jpeg) ![IMG_1325.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/23xyVECe3hZ6TTozXexgMxQ7QZs1YMpxV8yPVdVV2SN1d1oHGFmg2tKCdRYhz2EZMaVhC.jpeg) ![IMG_1324.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpEHik6Vn1r5WvfCeBwgpZEJ3Lhbv5dAVmSgVfFWK7Ds68zRo1KHEoTzM2TZTWMomvY.jpeg) _______________
While I was there, and since I love everything about religion, culture, and going on walks—whether in the city or out in nature—one of my outings was to the Christ of Vung Tau (Tượng Chúa Kitô Vua). Of course, it reminded me of the one in Rio de Janeiro because it’s very similar: it stands high up with its arms outstretched. The only difference is that in Rio you take a cable car or a little train up, whereas here you have to hike up a pretty steep climb. I walked there from my accommodation, the three-star Hotel Rex, which became my little home and refuge for the seven days I stayed in the city, a bit removed from all the hustle and bustle. The trail ran entirely along the coast, a beautiful seaside promenade. The day was a little cloudy; maybe it would have been better if it had been clear, but I still enjoyed it a lot. Plus, it worked out well for me because it was very hot, and if the sun had been beating down, I might not have been able to handle the hike.
> Estando ahí, y aprovechando que me encanta todo el tema de la religión, la cultura y hacer caminatas tanto urbanas como naturales, una de mis salidas fue hacia el Cristo de Vung Tau (Tượng Chúa Kitô Vua). Por supuesto que me hizo acordar al de Río de Janeiro porque es muy similar: está en lo alto con los brazos abiertos. Nada más que en Río se sube con teleférico o trencito, y acá se sube caminando por una subida bastante intensa. Me fui a pie desde mi alojamiento, el Hotel Rex de tres estrellas, que se convirtió en mi casita y refugio por los siete días que me quedé en la ciudad, un poco alejada de tanto alboroto. El sendero era todo por la costa, un paseo marítimo bellísimo. El día estaba un poquito nublado; quizás hubiese sido mejor si estaba despejado, pero igual lo disfruté un montón. Además me vino muy bien porque hacía mucho calor y, si hubiese estado el sol a pleno, tal vez no me aguantaba la caminata.

Since I was alone, I noticed right away: if I stopped, he did too. I didn’t sense him as a violent person, but it did stress me out to feel like I was being followed. Luckily, when I reached the structure, there was a security guard there, since they make you leave absolutely everything in a locker and only allow you to go up with your phone and passport. When I asked for the key, I told the guard about this man; the guard said something to him in his language, and the guy left.

Después de gastar en eso y quedar bastante graciosa vestida porque nada combinaba, empecé el ascenso. A medida que iba subiendo, descubría distintos paisajes panorámicos y pasaba por diversas imágenes de la religión católica que hacían alusión a los ángeles, a la Virgen y a Jesús con José. > Una vez que llegué a la cima, vi que se podía entrar al Cristo, así que ingresé. I have very fond memories of this little adventure. Something similar happened to me at a Buddhist temple I visited nearby—which I’ll tell you about in another post—but it was on this hill where I felt most sheltered and supported. The energy of the entire mountain was so beautiful; I felt like I was in my own world, connecting with nature, the mountain, and the Catholicism I grew up with—even though today I have a mix of different beliefs.

[source](https://mybroadband.co.za/news/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Cipherlab-driving-licence-card-scanner.jpg) **Security for the business parks and residential estates need to come up with another solution besides scanning your personal id card or driving license.** Living in South Africa you often have to access business parks or residential gated communities and the one thing they all do is scan your driving license/identity card plus scan the license disc on your windscreen. Once this information is gathered then you are free to access the premises. Not that long ago one would have had to sign a visitor registry book in order to gain entry. This personal information data is obviously being stored somewhere and this is concerning knowing how important our personal data is to keep private. The Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) has raised issues after it has received many complaints recently. Some business parks even use facial recognition cameras over and above the scanning of personal information without your knowledge. The problem is this will have to change as data protection is becoming more and more relevant in our society today. Having your personal identification records stored by an unknown security company does not exactly mean it is safe and these all have monetary value for data companies. What is stopping them form selling it on because you have freely handed it over when gaining access to the business park.
[source](https://imagedelivery.net/5qURAb7TXvxVtPgefqdvfQ/814aa1c6-4c73-4d36-68b8-5048be40db00/w=444) **These types of online one stop shop quoting sites are making money not on just the commissions, but also the personal data you provide.** The amount of times we unwittingly hand over our personal information for example when we are seeking insurance quotes. We hand out our name, our address and personal identification every time we are looking for a quote whether we end up signing up or not. The companies that offer the 10 cheapest insurance quotes like we have HIPPO in South Africa are making commission off the insurance companies, but they are also gathering personal data in the process that is worth far more monetary value to data companies. In the future all of this freely handing over our data has to stop and will be in breach of the personal privacy act. Then again it is probably already too late because many of us would already have our information on some database somewhere. A quick google search reveals that your personal data with a photo and identification document or card is worth around $263 per year for these companies to use. I am sure if you are well off financially and are a target market for companies then that data is worth far more. I have mentioned this previously that companies used to run competitions with what was deemed good prizes attracting loads of consumers who had no clue their information was being resold and paid for the entire competition. I sued to think this was down to the marketing costs and had no idea the company was actually making a profit from these competitions. These days I try and avoid handing over any sort of personal information because you just know by doing so it will trigger spam calls that will be phoning for months on end. The last time I did this was at the local butchers who was giving away a car and now I just avoid these information grabbers. It always seems harmless yet we know what is happening behind the scenes as having a batch of 5000 consumers with all their personal information is a valuable commodity today. Privacy on a public blockchain sounds like a contradiction. With Zcash, it isn't. You can take a regular, transparent ZEC balance — the kind any block explorer can see — and encrypt it onchain so no one knows the address, the amount, or the counterparty.

The process is called **shielding**, and a lot of the newcomers to ZEC in this awesome rally we are seeing have never actually done it. That's the gap I want to close in this post.

I'll walk you through how to shield ZEC inside the LeoDex wallet in under 30 seconds, why this matters more in 2026 than it ever has, and a shortcut most people don't know about: **you can buy ZEC that lands shielded automatically** and skip the manual step entirely.

## Why Shielding Matters Right Now

Zcash supports two address types. Transparent addresses (starting with `t1`) behave like Bitcoin addresses. Every transaction is publicly auditable forever. Shielded addresses (starting with `zs1` or unified `u1`) use **zero-knowledge proofs** to encrypt the sender, receiver and amount onchain.

Right now, about 30% of all circulating ZEC sits in the shielded pool. That's a record high, and it's nearly four times where the number sat at the start of 2024. The shielded-supply chart is the single most-watched fundamental metric in the asset.

AI is making blockchain surveillance trivially cheap and big players in the space like Grayscale are talking about it. Pattern-matching transaction graphs across exchanges, salaries, supplier payments, and treasury flows is no longer a research project. It's a SaaS product and one query away in a Claude Code session. Anything you do on a transparent chain is fair game for that pipeline.

The fix for onchain money is the same fix that the internet needed in the early days of buying stuff online: encryption. The asset that ships with encryption built in is Zcash and that's exactly why its blowing up today. 

## What You'll Need

- [LeoDex Wallet App](https://leodex.io/download) (Windows or MacOS, no KYC, no account creation needed)
- Some ZEC, OR any other crypto you can swap (BTC, ETH, USDC, anything)
- About 30 seconds


## Step 1 — Open the Shield Function in LeoDex

![image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcohEwkyb3rKnBbUGS4x5iLPCz7ayQG3o45uRQ8WXtfoN/image.png)

Head to your LeoDex wallet and find the **Shield** button. This sits in the same interface as your normal swap and trading view, so you don't have to leave the app or switch wallets to use it.

If you already have transparent ZEC sitting in your LeoDex wallet, the Shield button is your one-click path to making that balance private.

## Step 2 — Enter the Amount and Confirm

![image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRSc5bmGZtEihZbdNiE1EU4RnqxzW3VsRqFQVpsX1k6z3/image.png)

Type in how much ZEC you want to shield. For this walkthrough I used 0.10 ZEC, but you can shield any amount up to your full balance.

Hit **Shield**.

That's the whole interaction. The LeoDex MacOS & Windows wallet handles the zero-knowledge proof generation and broadcasts the shielding transaction to the Zcash network. You'll see a confirmation that reads "ZEC shielded."

## Step 3 — Verify the Transaction Onchain

![image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRXNpp9KEYQVMK3BMf2Tp1ine7UbZpouVDjB36fEcEiBN/image.png)

*trust, but verify*

This is the part most tutorials skip, and it's the part that matters if you want to actually check what just happened.

After shielding, click the **Explorer** link. LeoDex will open a Blockchair link of your transaction onchain so you can watch it confirm. You're not trusting LeoDex's UI — you're verifying that the network actually processed the shielded ZEC TX.

The transaction will show as pending, then confirmed within a few minutes or less. Once confirmed, the value lives in the shielded pool. Block explorers can see that shielding happened but when you start paying/swapping from that Shielded balance, it won't be connected to your T address whatsoever. 

*Pro Tip: don't shield an amount and then spend/swap that exact amount onchain afterwards as it creates a clear trail to your T Address*

That's it. Your ZEC is now encrypted onchain. Welcome to encrypted Bitcoin.

## The Shortcut: Skip Shielding Entirely with Direct-to-Shielded Swaps

![image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmc1amPjVaq32SLovCE1d1KJGVUxaTM9Wr3fgTYRzLQq86/image.png)

Here's the part of LeoDex that almost nobody is doing yet.

If you don't currently own ZEC and want some, the conventional path is:
1. Buy ZEC on an exchange (lands in a transparent address)
2. Withdraw to your wallet (still transparent)
3. Shield it (the step above)

That's three transactions, two of which are publicly visible. Anyone scanning the chain can see you acquired ZEC, even if your eventual storage is shielded.

LeoDex supports **direct-to-shielded swaps**. You can put in 0.1 BTC, hit swap, and the ZEC arrives in your shielded balance. No transparent leg. No onchain record of the acquisition in your name. This is a UI flow that we've built seamlessly into the wallet. It is powered by our route providers at Near Intents and Maya Protocol. 

The flow:
1. Open LeoDex wallet
2. Select the asset you want to swap from (BTC, ETH, USDC, anything supported)
3. Select shielded ZEC as the output
4. Hit Review Swap
5. Confirm

The output lands shielded. You skip the shielding step entirely because there was never any transparent ZEC to shield in the first place.

## Why I Built This Into LeoDex

Most privacy tooling in crypto forces you to pick: either run a dedicated app/node just for ZEC or accept that your shielding behavior is bolted into a single-purpose wallet you only open when you want privacy. Neither of those is how people actually live in a multi-chain world. They want to open one app and *"wonderfully manage their crypto assets". Securely, privately and entirely onchain and on their machine. 

LeoDex's bet is: **privacy should sit inside the same interface where you do everything else** — crosschain swaps, trading, holding, paying. The act of shielding shouldn't feel like a separate ritual. It should feel like a natural part of navigating your crypto wallet.

The current numbers say the market agrees. ZEC has run from $380 to $615 in the last month, and the shielded supply keeps climbing. The thesis isn't "privacy coins go up." **The thesis is that encryption stops being optional once AI makes surveillance free**, and the assets that ship with it built in are the ones that get repriced.

## Try It

If you want to actually do this — either shield existing ZEC or pick up some directly to a shielded address — open LeoDex and run through the steps above. The whole flow takes longer to read about than to just literally execute.

The day after I returned from Ankara, I went out for a job very early in the morning. The sun was just rising. Istanbul hadn't fully woken up yet. The streets were quiet. People were just starting the day. At that moment, I realized once again that Istanbul is really a completely different city. Yes, it's very crowded. Yes, traffic sometimes makes people tired. But despite all this, the spirit of Istanbul is very different. It makes people feel alive.


![IMG_2396.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoeFNum2hvNDyVWPoQ3RHpqSxjSEXiqcjtdNcH6GtJgta3Tx3UhPtDLcxDCWQ1AAGPM.jpeg)


I left the house around six in the morning. The weather was incredibly nice. There was a slight coolness, but it was a coolness that opened up. The sky was deep blue. The sun was slowly rising. I was starting to be happy even while walking on the road. I took my tea and the toast my mother made with me in my thermos. I thought, "Maybe I'll sit somewhere." Because the place I'm going to wasn't open yet.

![IMG_2370.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EppHKkqtjKsQnMacfWg2uQfhR4pWsjcwE1GQFVnE9QCyVmL6gL2cRu21N5wV8VPekSL.jpeg)

![IMG_2369.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpV9CDuabK6MBVcJEXscNVtLUDkUrcXYtqDa8dLtFeGca6NRYg6D22RcMStogJBQ6XX.jpeg)

![IMG_2371.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpvbeMyFDxHJqvoWn6jwfgkvM6vux2KRMe3hmTBpLs8hnLkZyjoqj6pmGXw2LXj8diZ.jpeg)
 

I walked to Taksim. I was in Taksim for the first time in the morning. Places that were normally very crowded were empty. It was silent. It was peaceful. There were almost no people. It was very good for me to see that calmness. It was as if the city was showing its true face early in the morning.


![IMG_2372.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EqYmRaeZJwdqWXRrBGdaDbRhdEtfe5iH2ygp1TA4L2L1iCA931X3YAwx31aiwJyr7aU.jpeg)

![IMG_2374.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpLfTZd3wzYWAPwFxUoncG5mHEvxL2MjRTZ7AtMXLQvgDzNYu2zcyesHozFku3GycXG.jpeg)

![IMG_2373.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoEpVBrjh1BxY3dHyEPCsDSHrKV9TZi4AQMBrdKNBTCuz4aJRnc23QWcE4Q4BuDPT9z.jpeg)


I passed in front of the historical buildings while walking on the road. Some have just started to get sunlight. Those old stone buildings, wide doors, long windows... The history of Istanbul really affects people. I feel like there's a different story in every corner. I took photos. I wanted to record those moments. Because sometimes people don't just want to live, they want to remember that beauty.


![IMG_2375.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpEFvrjSe636kA7zRAzsaEnQ5jkio8DjzfNajJWJW58PAPnJHVZERq35dMdw29haciQ.jpeg)

![IMG_2376.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Ep3cuowNCDYdz2iXiBoWdv3BePTzst24YJRVieXWUgGAa6BDHaNAiZgf2NqtQezY9nS.jpeg)

![IMG_2377.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Ep9zYHbLR8YXymwprZqTgLLmrNd5P8WUdqM2b2DhkTaxCDDupgDq41crCqRWB3svGGC.jpeg)


I wandered around Maçka Park. The air of the park is very different early in the morning. The trees were swaying silently. The sounds of birds were coming. It always seems very interesting to me that there are such quiet places in the middle of Istanbul. Huge city on one side, peaceful streets and parks on the other.


![IMG_2383.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EogMnYhtJW7RHpfkQTb9vzQg3fALuQ4pGpLFS2NmhfnDGpq9p1riESH9Li8pPzKxge3.jpeg)

![IMG_2384.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eos1KxLi6YKHX4nn78BMr5o8UM7VbXnW7HDfeHy7uFjyJUeswRCN7V9gcAWb9fc9dhJ.jpeg)

![IMG_2385.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EonkyhTMXtCUp4FTPxNJ7hWuAFqtqpusGCUYg8jUbASHWGMULLJrKVxWZDHcmufgdbh.jpeg)


After a while, I saw an Espressolab. It hadn't opened yet, but the chairs outside were standing. I sat down too. I took out my tea in the thermos. I started eating the toasts my mother made. I was really peaceful at that moment. People sometimes find the greatest happiness in very small moments.


![IMG_2381.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/23w2sMN1xKECjTpokRABVHMcC2og61emVYbutK9SepkVdugW1ms77dc56Rm9kJ7Kz7qJB.jpeg)

![IMG_2379.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eoke3gwSeqzV573DdZMrw4WkP7dzGBo7X1DbnasA3BF6fB22sdmy5mRMCNgn3SegJ8v.jpeg)

![IMG_2380.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoiW7tXsQFsxT1Ka7M3C8yaqEoGtWu14iYvMTUhBoguwGE65xCrBJ9FwAYcZy63EAfC.jpeg)


Then two of my little guests came. Two kittens. They were smaller. They were so sweet. First they looked at me from afar. Then they slowly came to me. So I gave some of the cheddar in my toast. They loved it so much... They both started eating with excitement. I think they are quite full. Having breakfast with them made my morning even better.


![IMG_2394.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoeEN34jL8QmRnGrMuKaBX31nyuMgahungcZ64JhvkCii7uRzjzTkDFyp5XxnzDQXeL.jpeg)

![IMG_2395.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EokdB1S1SrhYH8RWL7vXNRveWCRKeJ6zAvd3yxew1x8n1psRDdDA2uPJuqTSnFAiej1.jpeg)


Cats are like a part of the soul of Istanbul. It's hard to spend a day in this city without encountering cats. But I think it's a very good thing. One feels in a warmer place. Sharing the same streets with those little creatures always gives me peace.


![IMG_2401.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpvgTiCbLiNezdHquZuxDJYbCV1nevQjJNZq368rfqLpUqbuVVSfS5h62sMMToH9tWe.jpeg)

![IMG_2398.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpA1Uzv5SiJiyYYoR5ArfkXiAounMgme9Z5zQUACuRdpKAXGz2N9UB5ZL33ATWe7zDS.jpeg)

![IMG_2400.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eou7pJu5aMq5dP85MVUT97QSpEHX2KYpjmUtTWKWVydLyKNoukUv4m9y4kNHUkuertV.jpeg)


After breakfast, I started walking again. The streets were slowly getting crowded. People were going to work. The cars were multiplying. But I still had that calm feeling of the morning. I walked on the one hand and watched the surroundings on the other. Florists were opening their new shops. The grocery stores were arranging their products. The city was awake.


![IMG_2402.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EopsWC9EHzM9Nfo6waDUr3FgA2xgT2h8m4YXP7ChtYbDp8H23f7z6p5rJVnchiMsofY.jpeg)

![IMG_2403.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eou7J3xXB1WnN9XgyigZuog9m1Sdi7hMkRLaV8dtvURx8rT889ruRhq56Ap1CVYUdNm.jpeg)


I saw colorful flowers passing by a florist. Red roses, white daisies, purple flowers... Everything looked more beautiful when the morning sun hit them. Istanbul sometimes makes people feel like they are on the movie scene.


![IMG_2438.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/23xAZgWFwmZM7bPqChTDtBQziUVEphjkton19CbWVzXFCH2JFCeEJH1qm36yXAfPciXai.jpeg)


I really love Istanbul. I love it even though it's tiring sometimes. Because there is life here. There is movement. There is history. There is a sea. There are streets. There are people. And most importantly, there is a different story every day.


![IMG_2405.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eou9DyygVNFjfEKb3VWyvNdiNVArSitHcBswrAGg66AFoCLhRqCUtAdCjQAHRg8Cex8.jpeg)

![IMG_2404.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoiUgGBNL7qHxnGQXDUPB2f3LMM7jKrLeLFs6NnfCBYefoayRvXX3tJCyd8fJVF2VWQ.jpeg)


Right now, while I'm writing these, I'm watching the morning sun from my balcony again. The sky is slowly lighting up. I have a great feeling of gratitude. Sometimes in life you just need to know the value of such small moments. A cup of tea, a beautiful morning, quiet streets, two little cats... One should not actually look for happiness far away.


![IMG_2406.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Ep5mmmLoRpi2DY4eQY3rF4cZEYapVTR2M7dZTTumxuifptniddJk8Tw94jBKXfaVvmS.jpeg)


I thank my Lord for giving me these beautiful moments. I am grateful that I am healthy, that I can walk, that I can see, that I can feel. Because sometimes the greatest wealth is peace.


![IMG_2407.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoK7GS3BSjDSHrpErx2aaHFPBdMpoGcWBbXSnddfXQc98miB3oPjrYRAkjv51TXcoKN.jpeg)


If you come to Istanbul one day, see not only the crowd during the day, but also the morning. Walk on the streets very early. Get to know the city in its quiet form. I'm sure you feel the peace I feel too.

I wish everyone a very beautiful, peaceful and hopeful day 🤍

![Kopia – Beyond the route.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23xpJsE2RMAmsuEg8RfoQ7bymCj5sLFD6dArNo1uGuHqHA5YYbHXvP8jLR5F6TXCW2QjX.jpg)

There are places on the map of Europe that captivate you from the very first glance. Places that look so unreal that you start wondering whether that color of the water really exists. CAPO VATICANO is exactly one of those places. A small town in southern Italy that I had the opportunity to visit during my last trip. However, we did not focus on the town itself, but mainly on the coastline, which made us stay there a little longer.

As we looked at those cliffs and turquoise coves, we felt as if we had suddenly found ourselves somewhere completely exotic. And probably the best part was the fact that everything there looked so wild and natural. Without huge hotels, without crowds and without an overly touristy atmosphere. Just rocks, Mediterranean vegetation and incredibly turquoise water.

>Są takie miejsca na mapie Europy, które urzekają już od pierwszego spojrzenia. Miejsca wyglądające tak nierealnie, że człowiek zaczyna się zastanawiać, czy ten kolor wody naprawdę istnieje. Takim miejscem jest właśnie CAPO VATICANO. Niewielka miejscowość na południu Włoch, którą udało mi się odwiedzić podczas ostatniej wycieczki. Nie skupiałyśmy się jednak na samym miasteczku, a przede wszystkim na wybrzeżu, które sprawiło, że zatrzymałyśmy się tam na dłużej.
>
>Gdy patrzyłyśmy na te klify i turkusowe zatoczki, miałyśmy wrażenie, jakbyśmy nagle znalazły się gdzieś w totalnie egzotycznym miejscu. A najlepsze było chyba to, że wszystko wyglądało tam bardzo dziko i naturalnie. Bez ogromnych hoteli, bez tłumów i przesadnie turystycznego klimatu. Tylko skały, śródziemnomorska roślinność i niesamowicie turkusowa woda.


![20260417_135544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23uFPqVwaJiRGu1EcxuTpSSsE7W6K3i7LAsaMNPtZbQmududkVFiVC6upis4zt42DSPW8.jpg)

![20260417_135613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23ycwRBUqtJ9aa2qWg43hnLAY7TiTGb3H5c5cYFqJBzcMmRPVUSYd1JxDsVokAvoTSvSH.jpg)

![20260417_135518.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23vhs8xN4zyf7vCihS4eHKHZz1axVGzZreuJWCLTvSG5vbkHeAf4n1eCmNbe899rke8i4.jpg)

![20260417_140919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23y8j8v4q1HbUSm2bDC2gsXUah53MMVAi4N992GAdia3C1At75NhgpAZZ6UYqqcPMtRKC.jpg)

![20260417_140837.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23w2cjc2xTge758LQr2QdWP18hZPb3mGNy6sUsMau8TQ7ZgW1fZVTmR1DzxAYhy3ZcRhA.jpg)

We stopped in three different places. However, in each of them we found breathtaking views. Every single place welcomed us with beautiful landscapes. I definitely understand now why many people consider CAPO VATICANO to be one of the most beautiful places in all of southern Italy. I experienced it myself and I think this small town could easily become a showcase of the entire Calabria region.

>Zatrzymałyśmy się w trzech różnych miejscach. Jednak w każdym z tych miejsc znalazłyśmy zapierające dech w piersiach widoki. Każde z tych miejsc przywitało nas przepięknym krajobrazem. Zdecydowanie teraz rozumiem, dlaczego wiele osób uważa Capo Vaticano za jedno z najpiękniejszych miejsc w całych południowych Włoszech. Przekonałam się o tym na własnej skórze i myślę, że miasteczko to mogłoby spokojnie zostać wizytówką całej Kalabrii.


![20260417_140026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23ywipefXgHxWVy88MZ9X3oEsHgkq8o8wTzRYaTpjYkpex5Z8exoLy1KfFjVFhEjgyMSx.jpg)

![20260417_140944.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tmDLsYs7WNjyN8g5bpKM4F1E3RFvNLXFRexN8SCTQeVkqTKHur9mjniwRLjMtNRMtLx.jpg)

![20260417_140912.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/242XycfdDgK6EsECcVX8ECi8E3wKg64R38LdwfjmZnsPNRoQo2ZExjCtDCdt2dXrTJk9a.jpg)

![20260417_135627.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/244oSstNTfDuMj6HxpuKLJkPDX3uoTtDY3oUd3Uvf2jw17rtfRoGgbGCm7cr9XfyTg53g.jpg)

![20260417_135919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/EoyNXyrBwhsxysCfTKBT7shTZ1yTi4bTzvC9g79Q9dRbXsFSHtVZHZ7Y9sh8GxgZcn9.jpg)

CAPO VATICANO is mainly famous for its characteristic granite cliffs, which have been shaped over thousands of years by the wind and the Tyrrhenian Sea. This coastline is considered one of the most picturesque in the whole Calabria region. Many of the coves and small beaches were accessible mainly from the sea for a long time, which helped them preserve their natural and wild character until today. The characteristic turquoise color of the water is the result of the exceptional clarity of the sea and the bright seabed reflecting sunlight. On sunny days, underwater visibility here can reach even several dozen meters.

>CAPO VATICANO słynie przede wszystkim z charakterystycznych granitowych klifów, które były formowane przez tysiące lat przez wiatr i Morze Tyrreńskie. Wybrzeże to uznawane jest za jedno z najbardziej malowniczych w całej Kalabrii. Charakterystyczny turkusowy kolor wody to z kolei efekt bardzo dużej przejrzystości morza oraz jasnego dna odbijającego promienie słoneczne. ![COVER.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23s9dkXg1k7jwoQe7Nz3arde7564UsPhVm5JqyPsSsEq6Y8DZPDJ3WtjkKRwwCBLvL3Xf.jpg) ##### Hello everyone and welcome to my blog :-) Today I'm going to recount another episode from my visit to Marialva. When I arrived back at the highest point of Marialva, where the castle dominates the landscape, I already knew more or less what to expect outside. What I didn't expect was to find the gates closed. There wasn't much drama at the moment. I continued walking around the walls, observing the stones, as my daughter says, we've spent our lives looking at stones :) one day she will remember these moments fondly, although for her, for now, they remain just stones. Further on, besides the stones, I also observed the uneven paths and the open view over the village. Only later, back home, did I truly understand what I had left to see. ##### PT Hoje vou resgatar mais um episódio da visita a Marialva. Quando cheguei novamente à zona mais alta de Marialva, onde o castelo domina a paisagem, já sabia mais ou menos o que esperar do exterior. O que não esperava era encontrar as portas fechadas. Não houve grande drama no momento. Continuei a caminhar à volta das muralhas, a observar as pedras, como diz a minha filha, passámos a vida a ver pedras :) um dia ela vai-se lembrar destes momentos com ternura, embora para ela, para já continuem a ser só pedras, adiante, para além das pedras, também observei os caminhos irregulares e a vista aberta sobre a vila. Só mais tarde, já em casa, percebi realmente o que tinha ficado por ver. --- ![20260328_174022.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23uaD2gbGdrWWCpWJLeCa3cqaDWgtDTqNYpqPJoKcQZftLw4Ztw1vxqfQbt6ZrKQ2jQ5L.jpg) ![20260328_174304.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/2449x2BbGJobGim2AihVM92H1sDUZzbqs7Ny67FXbXGiRX71Zrrf5w69mqyGyVdVwC7Wp.jpg) ![20260328_174352.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23xVMJWZoE6ADsNXzCjKNNqY74pNue2rJYCTvNqozudikA28aGB1NkUNG1eMbTNNjBRFM.jpg) ![20260328_173527.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/244xnxSKC96ch9rujaFJ3WJjDsZhThXETQD2aV7nroaBgSupSd5JmQ6LX36BK7SAHisXN.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) Even closed, the castle is very beautiful. Not because of its size, but because of the way it occupies the top of the hill and controls everything around it. The granite walls seem to emerge directly from the rock, worn by time, but still solid. There are more destroyed parts, others surprisingly well preserved. The whole thing doesn't seem artificially restored, and that pleases me. It still conveys a sense of true ruin. ##### PT Mesmo fechado, o castelo é muito bonito. Não pela dimensão, mas pela forma como ocupa o topo da colina e controla tudo à volta. As muralhas de granito parecem sair diretamente da rocha, gastas pelo tempo mas ainda sólidas. Há partes mais destruídas, outras surpreendentemente bem conservadas. O conjunto não parece artificialmente recuperado, e isso agrada-me. Ainda transmite alguma sensação de ruína verdadeira. --- ![20260328_174440.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/245mq1wgdkhawXDmTwTC6CFC4WmSdTxNYJuX1E6BGHbX89GhxtDFZz486mZxUiJCMsjSc.jpg) ![20260328_174609.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/242NhKWhDeaGZWNHfmkHDfNfQBTePNBRYZk4soeUWEf94PspC88HpKqNAWRYaNCDVzmu3.jpg) ![20260328_175055.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/242rsEJuL7edxSUBKGdjWKxjrQeqhiA3mXt4LQiP6g1Xq2FcYNWYC5ZQKbm1vtWLt44GR.jpg) ![20260328_174858.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23v4VPWCaDp3LHQh7WP4TMQLdLiiTLkZZQEJCoXPhBGyxAFZU8ncwbjdGUY8fyAJ9b36V.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) The day was clear and bright, which made the stones appear lighter and the horizon more defined. From up there you see a succession of fields, small roads, and farmland scattered across the landscape. ##### PT O dia estava limpo e com bastante luz, o que tornava as pedras mais claras e o horizonte mais definido. Lá de cima vê-se uma sucessão de campos, pequenas estradas e terrenos agrícolas espalhados pela paisagem. --- ![20260328_175301.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/245HeZrxQfqQSibnxF4DkyZ3ixEg5ZVeFxKtdYLEoeWVwmYnmX1mKn45MJaHDxMXj2zrJ.jpg) ![20260328_175405.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/245mrdwgUV2KnyGzb5KXXNv1J5N96CZVV9CkmrqLAwYjzfsdMmKAEQxyhETDfv2PEdPAg.jpg) ![20260328_175222.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23ywnswsCE4czgdHeN7NtktFkxyWnpnWaMaWpbGGtiNjHxMdNe7S1FUCmZswJ9Sw85nzN.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) Around the castle there were few people. A couple was taking photos by the walls, and further down you could hear some voices coming from the village. Apart from that, silence prevailed. Not that kind of silence, the silence of an open space, interrupted only by the wind, the sound of birds, but mainly by an intense, yet distant, buzzing sound that I think comes from a beehive somewhere below. ##### PT À volta do castelo havia poucas pessoas. Um casal tirava fotografias junto às muralhas e mais abaixo ouviam-se algumas vozes vindas da aldeia. Tirando isso, predominava o silêncio. Não aquele silêncio, um silêncio de espaço aberto, interrompido apenas pelo vento, pelo som dos pássaros, mas principalmente por um zumbido intenso mas distante de um zumbido que penso ser de uma colmeia de abelhas algures mais abaixo. --- ![20260328_175410.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23r1iYuRWu9ajCX6jhods2ia6GgAxJNv7KWKrRfmEDZqWTCCXRyUoypvqvEKoFmXq4Yxj.jpg) ![20260328_175706.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/245T3Jwf8SBLRVJyrWEY6r7oqyEwZfw6vsEjxNhHz7bawGaXSYkT3FEQZHwojXfqMx7zT.jpg) ![20260328_175658.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23uaMQ4LtrXQyNbgZEhgTURb1VBwkNxmKnJcGm3kguqAeD7FGXhvy9BHw5Dm7LJrD2vR8.jpg) ![20260328_175432.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23rB5ea3TreeKqboN32MoA1zyxiUtf2LH8KoxfH9SyXr8xKNPpMxMxJFAphNyjtsQd48d.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) I walked slowly around the exterior, trying to peek inside through small openings in the walls and areas where the terrain allowed a higher perspective. It was already clear that there was much more than what the outside showed. Small stone buildings, internal streets, open areas within the walls. A kind of hidden second village. ##### PT Fui percorrendo o exterior devagar, tentando espreitar o interior através de pequenas aberturas nas muralhas e zonas onde o relevo permitia uma perspectiva mais alta. Já ali se percebia que existia muito mais do que aquilo que o lado de fora mostrava. Pequenas construções em pedra, ruas internas, zonas abertas dentro das muralhas. Uma espécie de segunda aldeia escondida. --- ![20260328_180051.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/2423o3QT4JQNJhqS6Gjwuu9iozoyzx6FKxp2bxPYy4XUuUUewfTEEWJgqYkrvcXFtaXT3.jpg) ![20260328_175924.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/244Uodf6ADBMcab4ws94Q3vpvu9icikRofrtUo1jXvParqJ5yTBFj7vRsy8cKYbU8G17r.jpg) ![20260328_180029.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23y8qrrpHYM5m52zyPwfaYrTDT5KVHpgHEe471V5ZUtechPNsqDE5RhgVAQJqQsY3B99z.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) At the time I easily accepted the fact that I wouldn't go inside. I thought I'd save it for another visit. But after I got home and started seeing pictures of the interior, I realized I had missed an important part of Marialva. It's not just about visiting a castle. Inside, there's practically a different version of the village itself, more isolated and raw. And that stuck with me. ##### PT Na altura aceitei facilmente o facto de não entrar. Achei que ficava para outra visita. Mas depois de chegar a casa e começar a ver imagens do interior, percebi que tinha falhado uma parte importante de Marialva. Não se trata apenas de visitar um castelo. Lá dentro existe praticamente uma versão diferente da própria aldeia, mais isolada e crua. E isso ficou-me atravessado. --- ![IMG_4013.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23w2gkHZh256R1bdFahRv8BHcDq5EkACdY7ikQ3BVeYr2pkQmBdgPn97S1ZbpMUBXPduH.jpg) ![IMG_4003.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/242hSD6bgGnXE8ZernRSPtzh8XayjsKtpFLPrr4xZQaFG9FjgzREjG2tKKGxQ7Hzkn4R1.jpg) ![IMG_4006.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/244UextM6Br2PwGW73jmS9aChTM9fHXuatV64XUDvhv1s9H6aQ3U4tUNJYMHhTeVVSmRk.jpg) ![IMG_4012.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23vsLEFSrdGWWnLU3YMDTMbPatXapkrF9MaFiDf1KKgudL4KAY2zBsVN7S9oaZ93koMhz.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) Even so, I don't consider the visit a waste. The exterior of the castle has enough strength to justify the journey there. There's something very interesting about that structure. It doesn't try to become a spectacle. It's there, exposed to the wind and wear. ##### PT Ainda assim, não considero a visita perdida. O exterior do castelo tem força suficiente para justificar o caminho até lá acima. Há qualquer coisa de muito interessante naquela estrutura. Não tenta transformar-se num espetáculo. Está ali, exposta ao vento e ao desgaste. --- ![IMG_4014.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23ryxJ3mzyekVRA34JMETAGHDREUWCg83MAEBffEJY1BTJ152wwgCTtzn4FLiyD7KfhTE.jpg) ![IMG_4021.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/244UvEvF1tkcif2KKheGSnJ1SeAmpZCGgbcac7EXWEDYTesoTqWcpD2AcKBYJv82pJaPX.jpg) ![IMG_4015.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/2449xTDyrK76LaA7LjVe6p9XndTG7u5zj4ouxtF4ii3EuX3W6Vii22K2Tm5a31pMLFwYd.jpg) ![IMG_4020.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/245wMfWPcTjo9edKFgeXXHD8ZxhBKo3DG3cUyhMFx8J6J1cZjhnLGKKWG1kKge1Km2xP5.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) Near the exit, when I stopped near one of the more open areas of the walls. The sun was beginning to set a little and the light was getting warmer. In the distance, I could see movement on the road below, small cars crossing slowly, while up there everything remained practically still. ##### PT Já perto da saída, quando parei junto a uma das zonas mais abertas das muralhas. O sol começava a baixar ligeiramente e a luz tornava-se mais quente. Ao longe via-se movimento na estrada cá em baixo, carros pequenos a atravessar lentamente, enquanto ali em cima tudo permanecia praticamente imóvel. --- ![IMG_4030.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23sUP6B3ffpVYDENg4W1adcrKo75DzwKvyesAPQfqttjjfRErUgCHmsS4cbLDeFpdYHHB.jpg) ![IMG_4022.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/23xySdioDNDYpCciGEcX1E91SpBa67GUTYxzchLqQv3fnEPbmNes6ch1MEh2gFPW7ccm9.jpg) ![IMG_4027.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/244y1gGq7XNVN943SBw8BQMXPcsLMXTEx3ihFrQK678H7KaoRowWpMN51BHVfFGc76aus.jpg) ![Untitled-1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyfest/EnymeWrmhSU78wMzJahA3HNMn7fja3hxMQGfPEyMEZJM3KLTfXNA89yMUNpMgmZyvpY.png) It was perhaps then that I better understood the relationship between the village and the castle. Marialva doesn't only exist around the walls. It also exists within them. And I, on that visit, was right in the middle of the experience. So I know I'll be back. Existe também dentro delas. E eu, naquela visita, fiquei precisamente a meio da experiência. Por isso sei que vou voltar. Não por sentir que faltou alguma coisa de forma dramática, mas porque aquele interior deixou de ser apenas curiosidade. Tornou-se uma parte do lugar que já não consigo ignorar.

## English version
The Obispos Square in Cumana is an iconic site located on Santa Rosa Avenue; it pays tribute to Monsignor Sixto Sosa Díaz, who served as the city’s first bishop in 1923. Diagonally across from this square stands the Santa Rosa de Lima Church. Nearby are two local landmarks: the popular Radio 2000 station and The Copita building, home to numerous medical offices.
![1000115915.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23w2ieJiqsinTYavKvSD72Lr28HJstZTr2DXCxbkYwk8bDu62Sth7n2Lv71igMa7XdS6C.jpg)
![1000115900.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/1000115900.jpg)
The bishop’s bust was vandalized, and currently only the pedestal remains. Here you can see several well-organized green spaces bordered by concrete edging. I noticed plastic containers being used as seedling trays, which will soon be transplanted, so this garden is growing.
![1000115906.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23uFTYto7Ta4vTcV3Tg3bU37Yoxkao5ZHbCzbQYGXAxhZaX62WNi1Uq2xBA9KJxQR9GD1.jpg)
There are huge, shady trees, including some almond trees bearing fruit. I also saw flowering plants such as marigolds, petunias, bellflowers, and coral flowers, as well as palm trees and coconut palms. This square is triangular in shape, and although it is small, it is very striking because of its varied vegetation.
![1000115910.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23tmB3ShV7M8CvmX5C7tB7CGUVhfBRQcvjR5WbW7r62oyYWVCezd74sPp8ATEAamjAzDv.jpg)
On Sundays, there is a lot of traffic here due to the number of parishioners attending Mass. Right across the street is a mobile fruit stand, which is another landmark of this area. This plaza is very close to three others located in the same La Copita neighborhood, which is why it is referred to as the church plaza to distinguish it from the others.
![1000115890.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/1000115890.jpg)
![1000115894.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/1000115894.jpg)
Although there are no concrete benches, it is common to see residents bring their own chairs and sit in this square in the afternoons or during the frequent power outages. It is worth noting that while this space appeared abandoned for a time, it was revitalized by the community, as evidenced by the construction of planters made of stones—some painted green—and the aforementioned planting of ornamental plants.

## Versión en Español
La plaza Los Obispos de Cumaná es un sitio emblemático, queda ubicado en la Avenida Santa Rosa y rinde tributo a Monseñor Sixto Sosa Díaz, quien en 1923 fuera el primer obispo de la ciudad. En la diagonal de este lugar se encuentra la iglesia Santa Rosa de Lima. En sus adyacencias se encuentran dos referentes locales, la popular emisora Radio 2000 y el edificio La Copita, sede de numerosos consultorios médicos.
![1000115915.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23w2ieJiqsinTYavKvSD72Lr28HJstZTr2DXCxbkYwk8bDu62Sth7n2Lv71igMa7XdS6C.jpg)

El busto del obispo fue vandalizado y actualmente solo se encuentra el pedestal. Acá se pueden apreciar diferentes áreas verdes muy organizadas que están delimitadas por un borde de concreto. Pude contemplar envases de plástico, a modo de germinadores, que próximamente serán trasplantados, así que este jardín va en crecimiento.

Se aprecian enormes árboles que dan sombra, entre ellos algunos almendrones con sus frutos. Esta plaza tiene forma de triángulo y aunque es pequeña es muy llamativa por su variada vegetación.

Los días domingos hay mucho movimiento vehicular por acá debido a la cantidad de feligreses que acuden a la misa. Justo al frente se encuentra una frutería ambulante, que es otro punto referencial de este lugar. Esta plaza se encuentra muy cerca de otras tres que están ubicadas en la misma zona de La Copita, de allí que se le designe como la plaza de la iglesia con el objetivo de diferenciarla de las demás.

![1000115894.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/1000115894.jpg)
Aunque no posee bancos de concreto, es común observar a los vecinos transportar sus sillas y sentarse en esta plaza en las tardes o cuando ocurren los acostumbrados apagones. One thing you simply cannot forget when visiting a city is… enjoying its parks. The number of parks in a city can also serve as an indicator of how well-organised it is. And during my day in Ho Chi Minh City, I came across several parks tucked away in various corners; what’s more, they were all spacious, well-maintained and clean. One of the parks I saw was on my way to the beautiful cathedral. We walked quite a distance and when we saw the park, we sat down for a moment. At first, we only intended to sit for a short while. But, as time went on, it felt so comfortable. Although Ho Chi Minh is as hot as Jakarta, the presence of many tall, leafy trees made the air in this park feel refreshing. I was able to sit back and relax whilst enjoying the gentle breeze. --- ![IMG20260402122710.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/EokcavwhNwW9RatraGmybk5LhrwMnwcpyDMyumSWK2T9sGrytTyXEvR9ynbs2NzEANx.jpg) ![IMG20260402122732.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23wqiZz6iv1NPdE1DifWFNyy4hgDFwSrCmWLE6Jw3M2zDJyhqsEjHp18FUyAUQAjHncZq.jpg) ![IMG20260402115632.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xKramH4gB1aCifhREjrPGx21ecF2s22mZ27rqoEQDVypubKrTV3yB6vLjCzgaSofzTU.jpg) ![IMG20260402173621.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23wgHuxdHad756ckp5KZMxjHV5wNmmFDkLjXTgzo7dmV2keZdjYJienGGepYip1rrvQVg.jpg) --- The flowers were neatly planted, a group of elderly people were doing yoga amidst the park’s fresh atmosphere, and, to top it all off, I found a beautiful place of worship. Of course, I took a photo of it. It’s a shame the place of worship was closed; otherwise, I would certainly have gone inside first to have a look. I don’t know why, but I do enjoy visiting places of worship of all faiths. Proof of that is that my destination today was also a cathedral (though it turned out to be a no-go because it was undergoing renovation). --- ![IMG20260402115721.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/243fpYDXsU48KP1VgigeVG56L8kJd5tXUemjJFQVayb43wHFXm2TK8EwdBM4yqdhzPu1P.jpg) ![IMG20260402115736.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23yd1r67NgHb3ytqNpX2Qt27X5D5NfAtsz9SQQmHn7MjyNFbFk6p1T3PK4XQZnd2hLJUP.jpg) ![IMG20260402173101.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23tbuQmpJTCqVHybvicP7ANf97KorysZN6WiamSoTDPRS8eNJi6FcnCiGsDZB6anJKGBM.jpg) ![IMG20260402173451.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23vhyN4UzA7u1YevjZyLNtGCSmu1gpckvfvr5a2cn7ZXGX3JBhFaTCxxKQ4irkM8FkLYB.jpg) ![IMG20260402173616.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23yTcm4Y3qx3UNbKyk4XwGiLHMf9MHkXdZufpGjn13ydprWvUNWUsyYdsqgix1cXxfCN6.jpg) ![IMG20260402173118.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xATu52muRASiCjduWPRJHwuFU7ZN1XTv8UvBKGT4pKtNEeV9vmVg3wRjPpGkQp2WBGj.jpg) ![IMG20260402173047.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23vhwsJCDGgjKnyr86EK4ESxEb7FvedLVrNWxheNMhzxWNz194RTNxwpNTJfaUYGaRTYM.jpg) --- And as I sat down to rest, I chatted with my friend about life, about improvisation and development, and the dynamism of life that influences our way of thinking. It turns out we’ve come this far in our understanding of life. Even though it seems as though everything is just left to flow, nothing is devoid of meaning. Whether it’s me or my friend, we’re currently at a stage where we’re wondering whether we’ll eventually find our respective soulmates, or whether we’ll have to resign ourselves to living alone? We talked about so much more until the tiredness in our legs faded, and then we continued our journey. Thank you for reading my post, and see you in the next one. --- ---

![Jakarta (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wgMmYKw1jY9yVjmTBpXaQNWc4E3tgMmetmt7eY814v5Kzyxz7vy2bFxGWhNuefPYrZ7.png)
On Thursday and Friday, I was attending a Community Literacy Summit in Kediri, East Java. This literacy summit invites library owners, writers, and literacy advocates across the region and first of its kind. During this summit, there were plenty of activities including a walk through old town streets of Kediri and the heritage site called Setono Gedong. I have been to Kediri multiple times but only during the summit, I learned the history of the place and found a nook and crannies of the city that I never explored before. ![DSCF1574.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23xyLcj2p1opGgtGuqbr77SC6cdZ1DPDAVDS8iUyNZeGosxYV4h3ikSkXjbztdqtZQPoy.JPG) # Setono Gedong 12th-Century Heritage Site Our walk starts from the parking spots adjacent to the train station. It’s also close to Dhoho street which is connected to colonial era districts and shops. Today, it also functions the same as is still even more lively boasting an architectural style that spans from across generation. ![DSCF1562.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23tmHZn4jxgvA3HiUpzHyRYwDJQJRMmYmUQwHeqburuoXzAQGZAiUM9ZZ3tKWKdvfqnXJ.JPG) Honestly, I never thought that crossing the main station, I’d find an ancient temple dating back to 12th. The place itself is already filled with houses and cramped. You would never guess that there is such a site in this area. ![DSCF1579.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23y8zTtg1UTm4Ce7dmURmJ12kQVQ7TrW8iSs8KE5SBcGpW2aCGmYjL2FoGBP2S9NAjG6t.JPG) During the walk, we were guided by a local cultural heritage preservation community. One of the people was responsible for guiding us through the walk and told us the history of the street and around this heritage sites. ![DSCF1564.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23xL3ARQTrbpoRMPaWrk4AwKtVmdFu49PWYG9UKZNQfm5iRx9Q8eqDG5ASquVwyxfM6Sg.JPG) Today, this historical site is connected to a major mosque in the area and is also a place of resting for an islamic scholar. When visiting the area, we could see the cross between hindu, buddhism and islamism all together in this 3 hectare area. The guide was explaining many things under the heat of Kediri and all participants including myself were very intrigued. ![DSCF1594.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23x1BPnPpoy9BoaFrRxUMZ6eUWvDNwMaCD4qhvJyiJYEhQRcAoMckC4QZga26SF6wK1Nb.JPG) Once we reached the temple area, I noticed some oddities. Typically, in a temple they are kept as is but in this temple, on top of it sit a traditional javanese pavilion. So, many of the participants including myself were guessing what happened to the temple.
![DSCF1589.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23xVEmiyjvdfGxKgjy3BHe6ZHADoobyz6LrWvczJZ1c7bvd9hAa3MK2XpCvN4yK6uycH7.JPG)
![DSCF1591.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23zGaHWwJn9Lm6WZ5U1LcRvStRsTDy11N5RqYTuPwzs4aN9wfrmZCbU6zzRFewu8VNdbC.JPG)
I struck up a conversation with another participant who was as puzzled as I did. We examined together that these stones are actually temples similar to what we typically find in Magelang or Yogyakarta. It is very unfortunate that some of the stones are vandalized. Well, I won’t bore you with the details but back in the day, there was no regulation nor was it something very usual for people to just pick the stone and use it to build their homes. ![DSCF1590.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23u63ADiCM3NZ4zgDXG8bb7z6CrRbYeyXmMWpa1xxwxzvhZJwocVjVxju9hEDPSM11G6v.JPG) For someone who used to be so engrossed with these types of architecture and history, It felt quietly sad that we will never see this temple in its majestic form.
![DSCF1593.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23w2mLPhN8CT1XPqFjuNiTq4NawF7PU4E23JFWB9v51m5qr4r2vfpYP3bcNiiRwGRCopo.JPG)
![DSCF1603.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wMQ8b8xoG1Xcot5U1XuzSrJ7rsAp2PWwzZKxzPhTXcmEF1crruadAoaU2kYYLu4G5ZR.JPG)
## Once we finished exploring this site, we were then taken to another side of this alleyway to the chinatown of Kediri. The Chinatown around here does not feel like it’s Chinatown. However, some efforts to restore the area are seen throughout some of its alleyways. There are many houses in this area that are still kept as is and have some distinct features unlike modern houses. I’ve been to many Chinatowns in Indonesia but this one felt more subdued than many spots throughout Indonesia. ![DSCF1621.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23xyQku6EfNMrq21eX6ddbncycq7UiKCAVqeKrd4ekjAJxHrwDKGhQrderNFzmCrrYTo9.JPG) But there’s one spot that shows Chinese influence in this area. Kediri is known for its tofu production which has a distinct color and distinct savory flavor. Its local name is derived from Hokkien and has existed since around the 19th century. We were taken to the first place where they produced tofu known as Tahu Takwa called Lauw Soen Hok ( known as Bah Kacung). ![DSCF1610.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23vPLiWCGb4GZE3zRLnKSvUkf4GUQoQjKRy69CKdXWMhUBjNxP9WUy2AqoCLSEmcPEjGY.JPG) Here are some more shots from around the place that felt like time stood still. ![DSCF1611.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23y8xK1DpAmw5aF6CsKRo5ET2yH4PkTwi6Tbd6bTCVKwjJ91YAgGWYg2fjmhXR6oPq3Yu.JPG) ![DSCF1617.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wMRdpjMaSw8U8mWaDWjDxrQ3FrMRqaMCcpnKLeThp1UEAphmVP616U2W1bGbSVMkkjW.JPG) From the pioneer of tofu production in Kediri, we were taken to the estate of an influential and wealthy Chinese merchant. Today his house is home to local government buildings and services. We were also told about the opium trade and history surrounding it including how the sugarcane factory was the underbelly of it all. While it isn’t something new to me given I visited many museums and learned about the story, it felt like another flashback and re-learning about the opium trades that funded the colonial government back in those days. ![DSCF1627.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wWuAn1xErBmVahwbQnGqfBL8i7VgpvHuBvXJxm5TCbRFRqd6SRvWmZFGKew8dHoMWH1.JPG) ![DSCF1629.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23vrtpCYXxiQ77Vj93cjs3toByoU4CXZaYLhNmCRqnQ93j9YmeM9pkxGbBKjSECkVd52Q.JPG) ### Free Morning Coffee ![DSCF1637.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wr3gAcKZNDAb3FpFzKM9m7bThpodwc6snKhAAHVUPikHCBtPzLyi2q3Dxy6u8gWhgaJ.JPG) We finished the journey visiting a street that is now famous for its morning coffee spots. We were given 25000 IDR worth of vouchers to spend in the area. There were plenty of options and I chose to spend it on a cold americano. It was so refreshing after the long walks under the heat. ![DSCF1650.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wquASyyMUxEaFMkMLR8oZBVi6KkeH3gFSMMJUz6nkmCZx2TUio6VcYsJ279TtrZ1eMS.JPG) I planned on visiting more places but in the end, I decided to just go back home after the summit cause I was exhausted. ![DSCF1664.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wfquZqLzY52cAJN1RUXp8c5NVu51BXUpAeZHVGcrq2qUnvYjFhinzBKzzmeEevqnJXS.JPG) See you in my next adventure! ||| |-|- ![NTy4GV6ooFRmaCXZ8UYgPhoud1kjiNX8QokLEZtbBKLuLWQ9yt7K3o4PG7qiS2SfyUvr6dYces7DWJ8xfHhq8PVtQPrvofyP72KL3ppdRxeugWvBfxeBRgtHv4FSStZc4YZ6Tzt1Pm995NNPZRyGjU7WNd7xvdEv2qtUNXuG.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23t77FQVTCGtEBi1QzCfnjLFZ3BpB57ocvnKWNZbybVoNT2WGNztX9UKrTyCVdjXyPVch.jpg)|

It is our second day here in Bantayan as residents, not as tourists. While we enjoyed our vacation here last month, I believe we'll enjoy the island more this time knowing we have a lot of time to discover the corners of this island as we learn to live like how Bantayanons do. My work will start three days from now, so I have plenty of time to enjoy the island more before starting my work, which means losing my precious vacant time and hoping rest days will come.
